text:
jamie: alert: sudden spike in 5xx + gateway timeouts on /v1/generate starting ~09:05 UTC. batcher queues ballooning on one shard. paging infra-sre. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0346 created 1: Elevated inference errors and timeouts. Severity P2.
pagerduty-bot: Notifying oncall. Please acknowledge: @leah.
leah: acked. i'm pulling graphs and logs. which region?
jamie: us-west-2 primary. seeing a single scheduler pod with queue ~1.3k, others <200. overall 5xx moved from 0.1% -> ~7.5% in 8m. tail lat > 6s.
mike: runtime dashboard: scheduler-batcher-2 pinned to a few heavy clients. ingress shows many long-context requests (seq_len > 6k) clustered to same shard id.
sarah: no prod deploys in the last 24h per deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: No production deployments for redwood-runtime in the last 24h.
jamie: grabbing scheduler logs now. scheduler-batcher-2 tail:
```
2026-03-14T09:02:58Z batch_accept queued=1324 inflight=58 flush_delay=1.9s
2026-03-14T09:03:20Z backend: downstream 504s from model-worker-7
2026-03-14T09:04:10Z batch_dispatch blocked waiting for kvcache; retrying
```
leah: can we temporarily triage by limiting huge requests at the gateway and preferentially routing small requests?
mike: quick counts: 
```
jq '.req | select(.seq_len >= 6000)' /var/log/ingress/requests.json | wc -l
```
-> 94 in last 10m, many from same client ids.
leah: immediate plan: 1) edge rule to 429 requests with seq_len > 6000, 2) reduce max_batch for scheduler-batcher-2, 3) spin up +2 scheduler replicas, 4) route a slice of small-req traffic to reserved pool. Implement 1-3 now.
jamie: agree. assign actions: @leah edge rule, @mike change batch config + scale, @sarah check dedicated pool capacity.
leah: applying WAF rule RL-2026-104: block/429 header X-Seq-Len >= 6000 with Retry-After:20 for now. Monitoring.
mike: patching scheduler env MAX_BATCH=64 on scheduler-batcher-2 to force faster flush. issuing kubectl patch now.
ops-bot: HPA scaling: scheduler deployment scaling from 3 -> 5 pods.
mike: new schedulers joining, queue redistribution starting. batch queue on affected pod dropping: 1324 -> ~180 within 80s.
sarah: dedicated pool has spare capacity. routing 5% of small-req flow to dedicated-prod-A. applying route rule.
jamie: we're still seeing intermittent gateway 502s between scheduler and model-worker; checking worker logs for OOMs or GC stalls.
mike: model-worker-7 logs show spikes in memory use, occasional OOMKills tied to long contexts. bumping worker memory to 1.4x and rolling restart.
ops-bot: RollingRestart initiated for model-worker deployment (memory increase applied).
leah: edge rule is rejecting ~1.8% of total traffic, primarily the offending long-context clients; their requests failing with 429 now. good signal.
mike: after memory bump + scaling + edge rule, error rate reduced from 7.5% -> 1.1% in 12m. P95 latency back under 300ms.
customer-ops: preparing incident blurb for affected customers: estimated impacted requests ~3.5% of total, mostly few enterprise accounts using extended contexts. drafting now.
jamie: root-cause hypothesis: several large-sequence requests from a small set of clients hashed to the same scheduler shard, creating head-of-line blocking; large batches caused model-worker memory pressure leading to OOMs and 5xxs.
leah: proposed post-incident items: - gateway hard cap with clear error message + docs for seq_len limits (owner: api-gateway) - per-client long-context quota and progressive throttling (owner: product/customer-ops) - shard-hash redistribution & soft-affinity improvements to avoid concentration (owner: runtime) - alerting: per-pod batch-queue > 400 for >5m (owner: observability) - e2e test for uneven client hashing (owner: eng-sre)
mike: opening runtime PR for adaptive hashing and per-shard queue metrics (will include per-shard queue-length dashboard).
sarah: created routing rule monitor for dedicated pool failover and capacity alarms.
jamie: status: mitigations in place, monitoring for regression. will stay in watch for 90m. handoff plan after that.
leah: i'm taking first-watch for 1.5h, then handoff to @mike for overnight. leaving notes in the postmortem draft. key tolerances: keep anti-long-request rule for 24h and monitor rejected client counts.
mike: added helper commands to thread for postmortem ops:
```
# find long requests and client ids
jq '.req | select(.seq_len >= 6000) | {ts, client_id, seq_len}' /var/log/ingress/requests.json | head -n 100
# scheduler queues
kubectl get pods -l app=scheduler -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount} {.metadata.labels.shard}\n{end}'
```
incident-bot: INC-2026-0346 status -> Mitigated; assigned postmortem task force.
customer-ops: final customer blurb sent to affected accounts at 11:20 UTC.
jamie: follow-ups logged: RED-1301 (gateway seq cap + UX), RED-1302 (runtime shard distribution), RED-1303 (per-client quotas). owners assigned.
leah: handing off watch to @mike at 11:35 UTC. keeping channel updated if anything changes.
mike: acknowledged, will monitor overnight. :thumbsup:
